challenges.title: A page object and isolated login tests
challenges.prompt: Implement LoginPage (locators for the Email and Password fields, the Sign in button and the alert; a login() method that returns self), then run the three login cases in fresh browser contexts. A deliberately wrong expectation shows how a failure is reported.
challenges.starter:
from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright, expect LOGIN_HTML = '
\n

\n' class LoginPage: def __init__(self, page): self.page = page # create locators for: Email field, Password field, the "Sign in" button and the alert message # (use get_by_label, get_by_role) -- locators are lazy, so it is fine to build them here def login(self, email, password): # fill both fields, click the button and return self so calls can be chained return self def check(name, fn): try: fn() print("PASS", name) except AssertionError: print("FAIL", name) with sync_playwright() as p: browser = p.chromium.launch() for email, pw, expected in [("ada@example.com", "s3cret", "Welcome, Ada"), ("ada@example.com", "wrong", "Invalid credentials"), ("", "", "Invalid credentials")]: context = browser.new_context() # fresh, isolated state per test page = context.new_page() page.set_content(LOGIN_HTML) page.set_default_timeout(1000) expect.set_options(timeout=1000) lp = LoginPage(page).login(email, pw) check(f"login({email or 'empty'!r}, {pw or 'empty'!r})", lambda: expect(lp.message).to_have_text(expected)) context.close() # a deliberately wrong expectation shows how a failing check is reported context = browser.new_context(); page = context.new_page(); page.set_content(LOGIN_HTML) expect.set_options(timeout=500) check("expects wrong text", lambda: expect(LoginPage(page).login("ada@example.com", "s3cret").message).to_have_text("Goodbye")) browser.close()
challenges.expected:
PASS login('ada@example.com', 's3cret')
PASS login('ada@example.com', 'wrong')
PASS login('empty', 'empty')
FAIL expects wrong text
challenges.solution:
from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright, expect LOGIN_HTML = '
\n

\n' class LoginPage: def __init__(self, page): self.page = page self.email = page.get_by_label("Email") self.password = page.get_by_label("Password") self.submit = page.get_by_role("button", name="Sign in") self.message = page.get_by_role("alert") def login(self, email, password): self.email.fill(email) self.password.fill(password) self.submit.click() return self def check(name, fn): try: fn() print("PASS", name) except AssertionError: print("FAIL", name) with sync_playwright() as p: browser = p.chromium.launch() for email, pw, expected in [("ada@example.com", "s3cret", "Welcome, Ada"), ("ada@example.com", "wrong", "Invalid credentials"), ("", "", "Invalid credentials")]: context = browser.new_context() # fresh, isolated state per test page = context.new_page() page.set_content(LOGIN_HTML) page.set_default_timeout(1000) expect.set_options(timeout=1000) lp = LoginPage(page).login(email, pw) check(f"login({email or 'empty'!r}, {pw or 'empty'!r})", lambda: expect(lp.message).to_have_text(expected)) context.close() # a deliberately wrong expectation shows how a failing check is reported context = browser.new_context(); page = context.new_page(); page.set_content(LOGIN_HTML) expect.set_options(timeout=500) check("expects wrong text", lambda: expect(LoginPage(page).login("ada@example.com", "s3cret").message).to_have_text("Goodbye")) browser.close()
challenges.explain: The page object owns the locators and actions; tests only describe intent. Each case gets a new context for isolation, and expect() retries until the message appears. Verified by running the solution with Playwright for Python and Chromium.
